    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Repeat each non-background object in the upper-left panel by translating
    # it into the other three panels, preserving the original panel dimensions.
    sr = next(r for r, row in enumerate(grid) if all(x == 4 for x in row))
    sc = next(c for c in range(w) if all(grid[r][c] == 4 for r in range(h)))
    tile = [row[:sc] for row in grid[:sr]]
    # The demo reveals a mirror/repetition pattern in the surrounding blank margin:
    # tile repeats at offsets of its own full dimensions, with zero/background retained.
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    for r in range(h):
        if r == sr: continue
        for c in range(w):
            if c == sc: continue
            rr = r % sr
            cc = c % sc
            # Alternating reflected copies: neighboring panels flip the tile axis.
            if (r // sr) % 2: rr = sr - 1 - rr
            if (c // sc) % 2: cc = sc - 1 - cc
            out[r][c] = tile[rr][cc]
    return out

 "content": "def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Identify full-length separator bands (the most frequent non-background color).
    from collections import Counter
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    sep = counts.most_common(1)[0][0]
    rows = [r for r, row in enumerate(grid) if all(v == sep for v in row)]
    cols = [c for c in range(w) if all(grid[r][c] == sep for r in range(h))]
    # bands divide a repeating pattern; the populated tile immediately before
    # the first separator is the template, repeated periodically everywhere.
    sr, sc = rows[0], cols[0]
    tile = [row[:sc] for row in grid[:sr]]
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    for r in range(h):
        if r in rows: continue
        for c in range(w):
            if c in cols: continue
            out[r][c] = tile[r % sr][c % sc]
    return out
"
}
